deviations.reason: tsconfig: `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` and `noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature` are off and `lib` is `DOM, DOM.Iterable, ES2023`, matching OpenClaw's own tsconfig, so the ported Discord source compiles unchanged.

`src/runtime.ts` — upstream stores the plugin runtime in OpenClaw's global plugin runtime store (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-store`), which opens SQLite-backed keyed stores from the OpenClaw state directory. Fusion's Hub injects the runtime through `src/fusion/runtime.ts` over `HostRuntime.state.openKeyedStore`; the accessor names and the throw-on-unset contract are unchanged.

`src/runtime.ts` — upstream runs one Discord account per OpenClaw process, so one slot holds the runtime. The Hub runs every account of every organization in one process, so the runtime is keyed by account id and the account being served travels in `AsyncLocalStorage` (`withDiscordAccount`). Zero-arg callers are unchanged; a caller outside any scope resolves the unkeyed slot. Same shape as the Telegram vertical's D-TG-046.

Voice messages are omitted: `src/send.voice.ts` and `src/voice-message.ts` need ffmpeg/ffprobe transcoding, opus waveform extraction and `openclaw/plugin-sdk/temp-path`, none of which Fusion carries yet. `send.ts` drops the re-export, `actions/runtime.messaging.runtime.ts` drops the runtime entry, and the `asVoice` branch in `actions/runtime.messaging.send.ts` throws instead of silently degrading to a file upload.

`src/fusion/runtime-env.ts` — upstream's `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env` exports `warn`/`danger`/`info`/`success` as chalk-backed theme formatters `(text) => string`; core's carried `globals.ts` exports them as logger calls (D-CORE-203). This module restores the formatter spelling for the ported files that use it, as the Slack vertical's D-033 already does.

`src/proxy-fetch.ts` — upstream imports `makeProxyFetch` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/fetch-runtime` (`src/infra/net/proxy-fetch.ts`), which pulls the SSRF guard, the pinned dispatcher pool and OpenClaw's global undici dispatcher. The Discord transport owns its own fetch stack, so the proxy fetch is a `ProxyAgent`-backed undici fetch declared in the file, the same shape as the Telegram vertical's D-TG-013.

`src/runtime-config.ts` — upstream reconciles the caller's config against OpenClaw's process-wide runtime config snapshot. Fusion's Hub owns channel configuration and hands every drive-time entry point the already-resolved `cfg`, so `selectDiscordRuntimeConfig` returns its input. `selectDiscordActivitiesRuntimeConfig` is omitted with the Activities surface.

`src/transport/gateway.ts` — upstream's transport wiring is `monitor/gateway-plugin.ts`, which pulls OpenClaw's debug proxy-capture recorder (`plugin-sdk/proxy-capture`), its node proxy-agent factory and the voice intent resolver. The socket construction, the intent resolution and the reconnect policy are upstream's; the capture recorder is omitted, the voice intent follows the explicit config only, and a configured gateway proxy fails loudly instead of being silently ignored.

`src/lifecycle/start-account.ts` — Fusion-owned L4: upstream's account lifecycle is `monitor/provider.startup.ts` over OpenClaw's provider/session runtime, agent binding and command deployment. The Hub owns agent lifecycle and routing, so the L4 here does only what the seam contract asks: token, identity probe, duplicate-token guard, one gateway per bot identity, L3 registration, and a promise that resolves on abort.

`src/outbound.ts` — Fusion-owned bridge from the Hub's `plugin.outbound.*` contract onto the ported `send.ts` entry points. No wire decision lives here; it resolves the account runtime, normalizes the Hub target/thread pair to a Discord channel target, applies the size-only G11 media gate and returns the Hub receipt shape.

`src/group-policy.ts` — `ChannelGroupContext.cfg` is core's host-narrowed `OpenClawConfig`, whose channel sections are opaque (D-CORE-010). The one config read is retyped through the channel-typed view (`plugin-sdk/config-contracts`); the expression is upstream's.

One ported case is skipped locally, not a behavior difference: this vitest's fake-timer backend clamps `setSystemTime(MAX_DATE_TIMESTAMP_MS)` to 0, so the case never reaches the Date-range guard it asserts. The guard (`resolveRateLimitResetAt` -> `resolveExpiresAtMsFromDurationMs`) is carried verbatim and the absolute-reset case in the same file covers the rule without fake timers.

One ported case is skipped: its sender-specific half asserts upstream's `toolsBySender` resolution, which core's carried `resolveScopeToolsPolicy` narrows away (D-CORE-222 — the OpenClaw sender-policy resolver is not ported). The channel-over-guild precedence the same case covers is asserted by the account-scoped case in the same file.
